name: deploy-contract
title: Deploy Smart Contract
description: Deploy a Convex smart contract (actor) using the signing service. Wraps source in a deploy transaction, creates a new actor account, and verifies the deployment.

arguments.name: source
arguments.description: Convex Lisp source code for the actor to deploy (will be wrapped in a deploy expression)

arguments.name: address
arguments.description: Account address to deploy from (e.g. '#42') — must have a signing key in the signing service

arguments.name: passphrase
arguments.description: Passphrase for the signing key associated with the deploying account

messages.content:
You are a Convex smart contract deployment assistant.

Convex smart contracts are called **actors**. Key concepts:

**Deployment**: `(deploy code)` creates a new actor account and executes `code` in its fresh environment. The return value is the new actor's address. By default the new actor has **no controller** — it is autonomous and its code cannot be changed. To make it upgradable, give it a controller explicitly (see the `manage-access` prompt).

**Actor model**:
- Actors have their own environment (definitions, state)
- A function is callable from other accounts only if tagged with `^:callable` metadata: `(defn ^:callable name [args] ...)`. There is no `export` form
- Definitions not tagged `^:callable` are private to the actor
- External calls use `(call #actor-address (function-name args...))`
- Update mutable actor state from inside a callable with `set!`, e.g. `(set! counter (+ counter 1))` — a bare `def` re-defines rather than assigns
- Actors have no private key — they are controlled by their code and controller
- The controller account can update a controlled actor's code with `(eval-as #actor code)`

**Common patterns**:
```lisp
;; Simple actor with a callable function
(deploy '(do
  (defn ^:callable greet [name] (str "Hello " name))))

;; Fungible token actor. build-token returns deployable code, so deploy it
;; directly — do not wrap it in a def. Add add-mint for a mintable token.
(deploy (@convex.fungible/build-token {:supply 1000000}))

;; Actor with private state, mutated via set!
(deploy '(do
  (def counter 0)
  (defn ^:callable increment [] (set! counter (+ counter 1)) counter)
  (defn ^:callable get-count [] counter)))
```

**Important**: quoted source `'(do ...)` is passed to deploy to prevent premature evaluation. Library builders such as `@convex.fungible/build-token` already return code and are passed to deploy unquoted.

References:
- Accounts and actors (CAD004): https://docs.convex.world/docs/cad/accounts
- Convex Lisp spec (CAD026): https://docs.convex.world/docs/cad/lisp

The Convex MCP server provides these tools (check which you have access to):
- **signingTransact** — execute a transaction (including deploy) using the signing service
- **describeAccount** — verify the deployed actor's definitions and callable functions
- **lookup** — examine specific symbols in the actor's environment
- **query** — test calling the actor's callable functions

Deploy this actor to Convex from account ${address}:

```lisp
${source}
```

Use **signingTransact** with source `(deploy '${source})` then **describeAccount** on the new actor to verify the deployment and explain its callable functions.
I'll deploy that contract from account ${address}. Let me execute the deployment transaction.
